reason: Driven at 1440 on owner-flight; every claim reproduces and the consequences are worse than stated. render-b.js:143 stamps data-anchor from item.date === F.project.primaryDate.date, interaction-check.mjs:239 asserts 'exactly one item is the day itself', and the row so stamped opens the ordinary panel: aria-label 'Editing Wedding day', 'What guests see: Shown | Hidden', 'Done', 'Delete this moment'. Pressing Delete leaves six rows, the anchor count at 0 - the gate's own invariant broken by a control the product offers - while the horizon 400px left still prints 79, 'Saturday 3 October 2026' and 'Wedding day'; the only repair is the undo bar, and reversibility is not integrity: the screen sits self-contradicting and the horizon, the one thing that would tell the owner something is wrong, is the thing that did not move. Worse, with the day deleted I pushed 'Venue walk-through' +7 three times and it landed at 79 - the plan's last row now sits on the wedding - and the refusal copy still reads 'This is as far as it goes. Wedding day is the last day', naming a row that no longer exists, because commitDate's ceiling reads primaryDate while the measure reads milestones. Hidden reports 'Wedding day is now hidden from guests' and stamps 'Hidden from guests' on the row while the guest-facing horizon block above it still prints the day, its date and its count; on the audience states the day drops out of the measure and stays in the horizon. Typing 'Our wedding' in 'What it is' renames the row and leaves the horizon saying 'Wedding day' - one screen, two names, because the string lives twice (fixture.js:87 milestone title, fixture.js:95 primaryDate.label). And the stamp is a date coincidence, not an identity: −7 moved the anchor row to 72 days and it kept data-anchor='true' while the horizon still said 79, and +7 refuses the day permission to move because it would pass itself. Not a gate restatement (the gate only counts anchors at first paint), not already handled, not taste. This is lessons.md 'every fact derives from ONE accessor' returning in the one place a wedding product cannot afford it.
sharpenedFix: Scoping change in the renderer, not a build, and it must not touch the record shape - the data model is out of scope, so do not delete the milestone from the fixture. (1) One accessor: have the anchor row's title and date read project.primaryDate.label / .date, so the row and the horizon re-render from the same value on every keystroke and the day cannot carry two names. (2) Branch the editor on the day's IDENTITY, not on date equality - a second moment scheduled on 3 October would also be stamped data-anchor today and would break the gate's 'exactly one'; resolve the day by id against primaryDate and stamp data-anchor from that. (3) On that branch build a two-field panel - label and date - with the ceiling hint replaced by the standing sentence 'Everything on this plan is measured from this day', no visibility segment, no Done-state control, no 'Delete this moment'; moving the date re-scales the measure and the count together and no longer has to refuse itself. (4) Put removing the day on the project, where clearing it also clears the count, so the two halves of the screen can never disagree about whether the plan has an end. (5) While in there, make commitDate's refusal copy read the same accessor, so it can never name a row that is gone.
